headline_format.first_down_scoring: YES -- rec_fd 0.5, rush_fd 0.25. Receivers are paid DOUBLE what backs are for the same first down.

key_confirmation_method: key_confirmed=true means a stat category of that exact name is PRESENT in data/fixtures/sleeper_capture.json, so the category has data behind it. false means the label was read off the screenshot but no such stat key exists in the fixture -- the category is in the rulebook and will score as zero.

categories_with_no_stat_data.SEVERITY: Low in points -- all six are rare events -- but the 40+ variants of the same three bonuses DO exist in the fixture, so the 50+ gap is a real vocabulary hole rather than a category Sleeper never tracks. The player-side special-teams keys are absent while the TEAM-side ones (st_td, st_ff, st_fum_rec) are present.
categories_with_no_stat_data.MECHANISM: compute_points_from_stats (sleeper_client.py:540) and score_projection (player_universe.py:194) both guard with `if value:`. A category with no stat data and a category measured at exactly zero are indistinguishable, and neither function can report which of its rulebook categories it received no data for. This is the absence contract broken in the scoring path -- benign for the arithmetic (0 x w = 0 either way) and NOT benign for knowing whether a league is being scored completely.

how_this_differs_from_greatest_show_on_p.pass_cmp: 0.1 here; ABSENT there -- ruled out by regression, see verification_of_the_other_league
how_this_differs_from_greatest_show_on_p.big_play_bonuses: 40+/50+ ladders on all three phases here; ABSENT there
how_this_differs_from_greatest_show_on_p.k_dst: neither league rosters K or DST
how_this_differs_from_greatest_show_on_p.WHY_IT_MATTERS: These two are the only leagues with captured rulebooks and they are not close to each other. Any engine behaviour validated on one is unvalidated on the other. In particular the receiving first-down premium (0.5, double the rushing one) is a structural thumb on the scale toward receivers that exists in THIS league's points and in no battery format.

verification_of_the_other_league.prompted_by: owner challenged the 5-point passing TD recorded for Greatest Show on Paper 2
verification_of_the_other_league.method: least-squares fit of the scoring coefficients against Sleeper's own PROJ column, 49 usable QB rows in greatest_show_on_paper_2_qb_proj.csv
verification_of_the_other_league.pass_td_CONFIRMED: free fit returns +5.20. Forcing pass_td=4 moves the median residual from +3.96 to -15.04 and the max to 31.98. The 5 is real, not a mistranscription.
verification_of_the_other_league.completion_bonus_RULED_OUT: adding pass_att (a completion proxy) to the fit returns a coefficient of -0.0077 and does not change RMSE at all (1.38 -> 1.38). Greatest Show on Paper 2 has no completion bonus. Fourth and Forever does -- the two leagues genuinely differ here.
verification_of_the_other_league.NEW_DISCREPANCY_pass_int: the capture records pass_int = -1. The free fit returns -1.47 to -1.50 across both specifications. Recorded as unresolved, NOT corrected: int is collinear with passing volume in 49 rows and a missing volume-correlated negative term would bias it the same way.
verification_of_the_other_league.residual_is_NOT_rounding: the capture explains its +3.96 median QB residual as 'fumbles-lost plus rounding'. The free fit closes it to 0.80 median absolute residual by pulling BOTH yardage coefficients below nominal (pass_yd 0.0394 vs 0.04, rush_yd 0.0961 vs 0.10). Coefficients biased low on both volume terms is the signature of a missing negative that scales with volume -- consistent with the fumbles guess in direction, but systematic rather than rounding noise. The stat CSV carries no fumble column, so it cannot be closed from the data in hand.

LIMITS: ONE league. The owner's standing caveat applies: league settings vary enormously and this is a data point for testing, NOT a benchmark. No engine constant may be calibrated to it. roster_positions is still missing, which blocks every replacement-level and surplus quantity for this league.

draft_math.ROUND_COUNT_CHECK: 10 starters + 11 BN + 5 TAXI = 26, and the startup ran exactly 26 rounds. The roster reproduces the draft length with no slack, which is independent confirmation of both.
draft_math.TALLY_DISCREPANCY: 312 picks are available; the hand tally of the board in evidence/roster_shape/real_drafts totals 310. Two picks unaccounted for -- either a transcription miss or forfeited/expired picks. Recorded, not reconciled.

IDENTICAL_STARTER_DEMAND_TO_THE_OTHER_CA.fact: Greatest Show on Paper 2 has the SAME ten starting slots -- QB/RB/RB/WR/WR/TE/FLEX x3/SUPER_FLEX -- so draft_room.starter_slot_counts returns identical values for both leagues (QB 1.85, RB 3.05, WR 3.05, TE 2.05) and identical league_starters at 12 teams.
IDENTICAL_STARTER_DEMAND_TO_THE_OTHER_CA.what_differs: depth (26 draftable slots here vs 29 there) and scoring (see how_this_differs_from...).
IDENTICAL_STARTER_DEMAND_TO_THE_OTHER_CA.WHY_THIS_IS_USEFUL: The two captured leagues are a natural experiment with STARTER DEMAND HELD FIXED. Any difference in drafted shape between them isolates scoring and depth, because the demand term the engine reads is literally the same number in both. That is a cleaner contrast than anything in the 33-format battery, where every format varies demand as well.
